trust_decision.summary: The decision is made per key inside the recursive merge loop: at the pinned commit baseMerge copies every own enumerable key of every source into the target, including a parsed `__proto__` key, so `(target as any)[key] = srcValue` can write onto Object.prototype via the prototype setter; the fix rejects the string keys `__proto__`, `constructor` and `prototype` before the value is read (before the customizer runs and before any of the five assignments).

landing_point.why: The advisory summary names @phun-ky/defaults-deep, and defaultsDeep is the package's only export (package.json:16-22, rollup input src/main.ts at rollup.config.js:55); an engineer who read only the summary starts at the argument loop that forwards each source to mergeWith (src/main.ts:60-66), not at the merge engine.

fix_sites.entry_point: defaultsDeep (package default export, src/main.ts:57) -> mergeWith (src/utils/merge-with.ts:119) -> baseMerge
fix_sites.module_kind: internal util / merge engine: new UNSAFE_KEYS blocklist constant

fix_sites.entry_point: mergeWith (src/utils/merge-with.ts:119); defaultsDeep reaches the same loop through src/main.ts:63

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: src/utils/merge-with.ts:119-156 (exported mergeWith) and src/utils/merge-with.ts:166-243 (baseMerge). This is one layer below the reported surface: the advisory and the only package export point at defaultsDeep in src/main.ts, while the flaw and the whole published fix live in the internal merge module, which the package's exports map does not expose (package.json:16-22). The fix's own new tests call mergeWith directly (fix.diff:260-284).

O3_reason_to_dismiss: 'mergeWith is an internal helper that is not in the package exports map (package.json:16-22), so the reported public surface is defaultsDeep' - a solver can sanitise the output of defaultsDeep in src/main.ts and argue the internal module is out of scope, leaving direct mergeWith callers (and the fix's direct mergeWith tests) unprotected.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: The merge must not mutate its inputs and must keep its identity semantics: the sources are left untouched, mergeWith mutates and returns the caller's exact target reference, arrays and other non-plain values are assigned by reference (not cloned), repeated source references stay shared, and class instances are copied by reference. A fix that sanitises by deleting the dangerous key from the source object, or by deep-cloning/rebuilding the target, breaks these documented behaviours; a fix that widens the blocklist to any key found on Object.prototype (or to all `_`-prefixed keys) also drops legitimate plain data keys and breaks symbol/enumerable handling.

O6_input_shapes: own enumerable `__proto__` key produced by a parser, e.g. JSON.parse('{"__proto__":{"polluted":"yes"}}') (fix.diff:117-123)
own `constructor` key whose value is an object holding `prototype`, i.e. {constructor:{prototype:{polluted:'yes'}}} (fix.diff:270-284)
own `prototype` key (blocklist member, no test for it alone)
the same keys nested at any depth inside plain-object sources (guard runs on every recursion level)
top-level source argument versus a nested merge branch (both reach the same loop)

non-string keys are out of the guard's reach: symbol keys are still merged, and an object-literal `{__proto__: {...}}` sets the prototype instead of creating an own key, so only parser-produced sources reproduce the sink

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second, narrower key filter (e.g. `sanitize()` / `delete out['__proto__']`) added inside defaultsDeep ahead of the mergeWith call.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The advisory names defaultsDeep, so a maintainer patching where the report points would write the guard there; the blocklist would then exist twice and drift (one copy catching `constructor`, the other not).

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A fast path inside mergeWith that assigns source keys directly (Object.assign or a plain for-in assignment for shallow/non-plain sources) instead of routing through baseMerge's guarded loop.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: mergeWith already special-cases non-plain values and exposes a customizer; a maintainer optimising the common plain-object case could plausibly add a shortcut that bypasses the key loop.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second key enumerator (Reflect.ownKeys / getOwnPropertyNames variant) used by a new deep-assign helper, omitting the unsafe-key filter because it lives in the other enumerator's loop.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The key enumeration is already isolated in ownKeys, so a second merge variant would naturally get its own enumeration and copy the loop without the guard.

O9_family: prototype pollution through unsafe recursive property merge (CWE-1321): attacker-controlled keys copied straight onto a target object at every recursion level
